name: blizzard_diffuse
about: Standardized recipe for the Blizzard / WoW-style stylized diffuse (TexTools 'Paint Base'), expressed as Patina ops. Run with: node tools/blizzard/apply.mjs <project.patina.json>

notes: top/mid/bottom stay in one hue family: only the value changes, plus a warm top / cool bottom shift. Cross-hue ramps read as airbrushed, not painted.
edge_lo/edge_hi/edge_blur are tuned for low-poly meshes (thin convex ridges). Raise edge_blur to 12-20 texels when the mesh is a fan-filled n-gon soup.

cavity_soft is the upper end of the window on the baked cavity map: 0.10 = hairline creases, 0.3-0.5 = soft fold shadows. A narrow window (0.08-0.14) clips the whole crease region to 1.0, so the bake's lattice staircase becomes hard triangular plateaus - widen it and blur (cavity_blur 8).

the Cavity layer must add its roughness, not replace it: blend_modes {roughness: add}. Without it a channel range [0, 0.12] writes 0.0-0.12 into every crease - mirror-polished folds, and a roughness map with std 0.29 instead of 0.03.

seam_* draws the painted outline inside each UV island border with the uv_stroke field: 4-8 texels at 1024 for a hand-inked edge, 12-20 for a soft airbrushed rim. It follows UV seams, so it also hides them.
roughness 0.8 keeps the albedo matte so the value ramp is what sells the shape; the studio HDRI still gives a satin sheen.
on a near-white albedo a white edge highlight is invisible: it lifts white onto white. Give edge_color a warm cast (#fff0d8) and put the contrast in hue instead of value - sun on white cloth.

curvature comes from the low poly unless bake.normal.high points at a dense mesh. With the low only, sliver triangles light up along their long edges as bright diagonals, so edge_lo has to stay high (0.52) and the highlight is coarse. Bake from a high poly and the map is clean: edge_lo 0.45 / edge 0.45 / edge_blur 8 reads as a crisp sunlit ridge with no breakup.

a high poly reaches the albedo mainly through AO (the cavity term), not through the edge light: switch cavity off in both bakes and high-vs-low basecolor collapses to 0.12/255 on input/sailor.glb. bake.normal.curvature is the knob that folds the dense mesh into the curvature field (8/255 at 1, 39/255 at 4 with curvature_gain 2; it clamps at 16), and the crease layer is what spends it: crease 0.55 / crease_lo 0.55 / crease_hi 0.85.

do not max the injection out. curvature 16 with curvature_gain 4 lifts the high-poly share of the albedo from 9 to 16.7/255, but the crease term (11/255) then reads as dirt rather than wrinkles; 4-8 at gain 2 is the last clean rung (input/ab_highpoly/ladder.sh). The rest of the dense mesh's detail belongs in the normal map.

white-grey ramps (bone / pearl / slate) carry the whole read on value alone: keep top near 0.9, mid near 0.72, bottom near 0.36 so the ramp still carves the form, and let seam_color sit a step darker than bottom so the outline survives on the light half.
